records.question:
Set $\gamma(x)\equiv 0$ and take the one-step source \eqref{eq:source}--\eqref{eq:S1}.
Solve for $f(q,x)$ and compute $Y_2(x)$ and $Y_3(x)$ explicitly. Show that $\bar q(x)=q_0$ for all $x$.
records.gold_answer:
\[
f(q,x)=\delta(q-q_0)\int_0^x A u^3 e^{-u}\,du,\quad
Y_2=q_0^2\!\int_0^x Au^3e^{-u}du,\quad
Y_3=q_0^3\!\int_0^x Au^3e^{-u}du,
\]
so $\bar q(x)=q_0$.
$\mathcal{N}=Y_2/2$ and the closed ODE system is \eqref{eq:moment_odes}.

records.question:
Take a two-step injection (mimicking multiple freeze-in ``steps''):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two_step_source}
\mathcal{S}(x)=A x^3 e^{-x}+B x^3 e^{-r x}\,\Theta(x-x_1),
\qquad A,B>0,\ r>0,\ x_1>0,
\end{equation}
with injection momentum $q_0$ as in \eqref{eq:source}.
Assume kineticization turns on only after $x=x_s$:
\[
\gamma(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,& 0\le x<x_s,\\
\gamma_0,& x\ge x_s,
\end{cases}
\qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and production turns off at $x=x_s$ (i.e.\ take $x_s\ge x_1$ and set $S=0$ for $x\ge x_s$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the post-production initial moments $Y_2(x_s)$, $Y_3(x_s)$, $Y_4(x_s)$ explicitly in terms of
$A,B,r,x_1,x_s,q_0$ (no unevaluated integrals).
\item For $x\ge x_s$, solve Boltzmann equation for the moments with constant $\gamma_0$ and write closed forms for
\[
\bar q(x)=\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)},\qquad
\mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}-\left(\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)}\right)^2.
\]
\end{enumerate}
records.gold_answer:
Define
\[
K=
A\big(6-\Gamma(4,x_s)\big)
+\frac{B}{r^4}\Big(\Gamma(4,r x_1)-\Gamma(4,r x_s)\Big).
\]
Then
\[
Y_2(x_s)=q_0^2 K,\quad Y_3(x_s)=q_0^3 K,\quad Y_4(x_s)=q_0^4 K,
\]
and for $x\ge x_s$,
\[
\ \bar q(x)=3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}=12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\left[12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]
-\left[3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]^2\ .
\]

Show that the coefficient
\[
c_N(D_{\rm tot},K)\equiv [t^{D_{\rm tot}}u^K]\,H_N(t,u)
\]
equals the number of nonnegative integer solutions of the following system:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diophantine}
\begin{aligned}
a_0+b_0+2(a_1+b_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N c_n &= D_{\rm tot},\\
c_1+\cdots+c_N &= K,\\
(a_0+a_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N n\,c_n &= (b_0+b_1),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\[
a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1,c_1,\dots,c_N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}.
\]
(\emph{Interpretation:} $a_0,b_0$ count powers of $X,Y$; $a_1,b_1$ count powers of $D,\bar D$; $c_n$ counts powers of $S_n$.)
records.gold_answer: $c_N(D_{\rm tot},K)$ is the number of solutions of \eqref{eq:diophantine}.

records.question: Given a composition $[n_1, \dots, n_s]$, what is $(D-2 \delta \circ S -2 S \circ \delta)  [n_1, \dots, n_s]$?
records.gold_answer:
If $n_s \neq 2$,
\[ (D-2 \delta \circ S -2 S \circ \delta)  [n_1, \dots, n_s] = 0 \]  and
\[ (D-2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta) [n_1 \dots n_{s-1}, 2] = \! 2 \sum_{1 \le k \le s} \! \! (-1)^{s+ k+ \sum_{m=1}^{k-1} n_m } [n_1 \dots n_{k-1}, 1, n_k \dots n_{s-1}] \] otherwise.

records.question:
Let $p > 2$. Take $x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k}  y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l} y_0$ with size $m$.
What are $(D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l})$ and $(D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l} y_0)$?
records.gold_answer:
\[ (D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l}) = 0 \]
and
\[ (D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l} y_0) = 2 (-1)^{n-m+1} (n-m+1) x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l}. \]

For $\mathcal{A}=\{1,3,5\}$ with $\sigma=4$, use the constraints to determine the unique coefficients $(c_2,c_3,c_0)$,
then write the final explicit $M(s,t)$ (you may leave it as sums over $a\in\mathcal{A}$).
records.gold_answer:
$c_2=-9,\quad c_3=-3, \quad c_0=\frac{2704}{55}.$
The final amplitude is
\[
M(s,t)=\sum_{a\in\{1,3,5\}}
\left(\frac{s^4}{s-a}+\frac{t^4}{t-a}+\frac{u^4}{u-a}\right)
+\frac{2704}{55}-9(s^2+t^2+u^2)-3(s^3+t^3+u^3),
\quad u=4-s-t.
\]

records.question:
Take a two-step injection (mimicking multiple freeze-in ``steps''):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two_step_source}
\mathcal{S}(x)=A x^3 e^{-x}+B x^3 e^{-r x}\,\Theta(x-x_1),
\qquad A,B>0,\ r>0,\ x_1>0,
\end{equation}
with injection momentum $q_0$ as in \eqref{eq:source}.
Assume kineticization turns on only after $x=x_s$:
\[
\gamma(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,& 0\le x<x_s,\\
\gamma_0,& x\ge x_s,
\end{cases}
\qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and production turns off at $x=x_s$ (i.e.\ take $x_s\ge x_1$ and set $S=0$ for $x\ge x_s$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the post-production initial moments $Y_2(x_s)$, $Y_3(x_s)$, $Y_4(x_s)$ explicitly in terms of
$A,B,r,x_1,x_s,q_0$ (no unevaluated integrals).
\item For $x\ge x_s$, solve Boltzmann equation for the moments with constant $\gamma_0$ and write closed forms for
\[
\bar q(x)=\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)},\qquad
\mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}-\left(\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)}\right)^2.
\]
\end{enumerate}
records.gold_answer:
Define
\[
K=
A\big(6-\Gamma(4,x_s)\big)
+\frac{B}{r^4}\Big(\Gamma(4,r x_1)-\Gamma(4,r x_s)\Big).
\]
Then
\[
Y_2(x_s)=q_0^2 K,\quad Y_3(x_s)=q_0^3 K,\quad Y_4(x_s)=q_0^4 K,
\]
and for $x\ge x_s$,
\[
\ \bar q(x)=3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}=12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\left[12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]
-\left[3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]^2\ .
\]

Definition (Cayley--Hamilton for $2\times2$): Let $U\in\mathbb C^{2\times2}$ and define invariants
\[
t\equiv \mathrm{tr}\,U,\qquad d\equiv \det U.
\]
Cayley--Hamilton gives
\begin{align}
U^2 - t\,U + d\,I = 0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
U^2 = tU-dI.
\label{eq:CH2}
\end{align}
Hence any polynomial in $U$ reduces to a linear combination of $\{I,U\}$.
Definition (Matrix power series and Fr\'echet derivative): For a scalar power series $f(z)=\sum_{n\ge0} a_n z^n$, define
\[
f(U)\equiv \sum_{n\ge0} a_n U^n.
\]
The Fr\'echet derivative (differential) of $f$ at $U$ in the direction $E$ is
\[
D f(U)[E]\equiv \left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\right|_{\tau=0} f(U+\tau E).
\]
Rindlisbacher emphasizes that the Cayley--Hamilton iterative method can compute both $f(U)$ and its differentials efficiently.

Show that the coefficient
\[
c_N(D_{\rm tot},K)\equiv [t^{D_{\rm tot}}u^K]\,H_N(t,u)
\]
equals the number of nonnegative integer solutions of the following system:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diophantine}
\begin{aligned}
a_0+b_0+2(a_1+b_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N c_n &= D_{\rm tot},\\
c_1+\cdots+c_N &= K,\\
(a_0+a_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N n\,c_n &= (b_0+b_1),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\[
a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1,c_1,\dots,c_N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}.
\]
(\emph{Interpretation:} $a_0,b_0$ count powers of $X,Y$; $a_1,b_1$ count powers of $D,\bar D$; $c_n$ counts powers of $S_n$.)
records.gold_answer: $c_N(D_{\rm tot},K)$ is the number of solutions of \eqref{eq:diophantine}.

records.question:
Take a two-step injection (mimicking multiple freeze-in ``steps''):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two_step_source}
\mathcal{S}(x)=A x^3 e^{-x}+B x^3 e^{-r x}\,\Theta(x-x_1),
\qquad A,B>0,\ r>0,\ x_1>0,
\end{equation}
with injection momentum $q_0$ as in \eqref{eq:source}.
Assume kineticization turns on only after $x=x_s$:
\[
\gamma(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,& 0\le x<x_s,\\
\gamma_0,& x\ge x_s,
\end{cases}
\qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and production turns off at $x=x_s$ (i.e.\ take $x_s\ge x_1$ and set $S=0$ for $x\ge x_s$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the post-production initial moments $Y_2(x_s)$, $Y_3(x_s)$, $Y_4(x_s)$ explicitly in terms of
$A,B,r,x_1,x_s,q_0$ (no unevaluated integrals).
\item For $x\ge x_s$, solve Boltzmann equation for the moments with constant $\gamma_0$ and write closed forms for
\[
\bar q(x)=\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)},\qquad
\mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}-\left(\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)}\right)^2.
\]
\end{enumerate}
records.gold_answer:
Define
\[
K=
A\big(6-\Gamma(4,x_s)\big)
+\frac{B}{r^4}\Big(\Gamma(4,r x_1)-\Gamma(4,r x_s)\Big).
\]
Then
\[
Y_2(x_s)=q_0^2 K,\quad Y_3(x_s)=q_0^3 K,\quad Y_4(x_s)=q_0^4 K,
\]
and for $x\ge x_s$,
\[
\ \bar q(x)=3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}=12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\left[12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]
-\left[3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]^2\ .
\]

records.question:
Take a two-step injection (mimicking multiple freeze-in ``steps''):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two_step_source}
\mathcal{S}(x)=A x^3 e^{-x}+B x^3 e^{-r x}\,\Theta(x-x_1),
\qquad A,B>0,\ r>0,\ x_1>0,
\end{equation}
with injection momentum $q_0$ as in \eqref{eq:source}.
Assume kineticization turns on only after $x=x_s$:
\[
\gamma(x)=
\begin{cases}
0,& 0\le x<x_s,\\
\gamma_0,& x\ge x_s,
\end{cases}
\qquad \gamma_0>0,
\]
and production turns off at $x=x_s$ (i.e.\ take $x_s\ge x_1$ and set $S=0$ for $x\ge x_s$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the post-production initial moments $Y_2(x_s)$, $Y_3(x_s)$, $Y_4(x_s)$ explicitly in terms of
$A,B,r,x_1,x_s,q_0$ (no unevaluated integrals).
\item For $x\ge x_s$, solve Boltzmann equation for the moments with constant $\gamma_0$ and write closed forms for
\[
\bar q(x)=\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)},\qquad
\mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}-\left(\frac{Y_3(x)}{Y_2(x)}\right)^2.
\]
\end{enumerate}
records.gold_answer:
Define
\[
K=
A\big(6-\Gamma(4,x_s)\big)
+\frac{B}{r^4}\Big(\Gamma(4,r x_1)-\Gamma(4,r x_s)\Big).
\]
Then
\[
Y_2(x_s)=q_0^2 K,\quad Y_3(x_s)=q_0^3 K,\quad Y_4(x_s)=q_0^4 K,
\]
and for $x\ge x_s$,
\[
\ \bar q(x)=3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \frac{Y_4(x)}{Y_2(x)}=12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\ ,
\]
\[
\ \mathrm{Var}_q(x)=\left[12+(q_0^2-12)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]
-\left[3+(q_0-3)e^{-\gamma_0(x-x_s)}\right]^2\ .
\]

Definition (Cayley--Hamilton for $2\times2$): Let $U\in\mathbb C^{2\times2}$ and define invariants
\[
t\equiv \mathrm{tr}\,U,\qquad d\equiv \det U.
\]
Cayley--Hamilton gives
\begin{align}
U^2 - t\,U + d\,I = 0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
U^2 = tU-dI.
\label{eq:CH2}
\end{align}
Hence any polynomial in $U$ reduces to a linear combination of $\{I,U\}$.
Definition (Matrix power series and Fr\'echet derivative): For a scalar power series $f(z)=\sum_{n\ge0} a_n z^n$, define
\[
f(U)\equiv \sum_{n\ge0} a_n U^n.
\]
The Fr\'echet derivative (differential) of $f$ at $U$ in the direction $E$ is
\[
D f(U)[E]\equiv \left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\right|_{\tau=0} f(U+\tau E).
\]
Rindlisbacher emphasizes that the Cayley--Hamilton iterative method can compute both $f(U)$ and its differentials efficiently.

Show that the coefficient
\[
c_N(D_{\rm tot},K)\equiv [t^{D_{\rm tot}}u^K]\,H_N(t,u)

equals the number of nonnegative integer solutions of the following system:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diophantine}
\begin{aligned}
a_0+b_0+2(a_1+b_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N c_n &= D_{\rm tot},\\
c_1+\cdots+c_N &= K,\\
(a_0+a_1)+\sum_{n=1}^N n\,c_n &= (b_0+b_1),
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\[
a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1,c_1,\dots,c_N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}.
\]
(\emph{Interpretation:} $a_0,b_0$ count powers of $X,Y$; $a_1,b_1$ count powers of $D,\bar D$; $c_n$ counts powers of $S_n$.)

records.question: Given a composition $[n_1, \dots, n_s]$, what is $(D-2 \delta \circ S -2 S \circ \delta)  [n_1, \dots, n_s]$?
records.gold_answer:
If $n_s \neq 2$,
\[ (D-2 \delta \circ S -2 S \circ \delta)  [n_1, \dots, n_s] = 0 \]  and
\[ (D-2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta) [n_1 \dots n_{s-1}, 2] = \! 2 \sum_{1 \le k \le s} \! \! (-1)^{s+ k+ \sum_{m=1}^{k-1} n_m } [n_1 \dots n_{k-1}, 1, n_k \dots n_{s-1}] \] otherwise.

What are $(D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l})$ and $(D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l} y_0)$?
records.gold_answer:
\[ (D - 2 \delta \circ S - 2 S \circ \delta)( x_1^{c_1} \cdots x_k^{c_k} y_1^{d_1} \cdots y_l^{d_l}) = 0 \]
and
